clue.text: 'He proposed a game at four-handed ——' (The Old Curiosity Shop)

definitions.text: 'He proposed a game at four-handed ——' (The Old Curiosity Shop)

parts.words: 'He proposed a game at four-handed ——' (The Old Curiosity Shop)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the card game played in Dickens's novel, scored on a pegboard

explanation.definitionFit: In The Old Curiosity Shop Dick Swiveller plays this card game, scored with pegs on a board, with the Marchioness.

clue.text: Many bid for Markandaya's sort of submarine equipment

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
to bid is to make an offer

explanation.surface: Lots of people tender for a piece of underwater gear described by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Kamala Markandaya, an Indian novelist, wrote The Coffer Dams; a coffer dam is a watertight enclosure used for building under water.
explanation.definitionFit: A watertight caisson used for underwater construction is a coffer dam, the kind in Markandaya's novel title.

clue.text: Nocturnal reptile from Tennessee

parts.note: not a creature of the American state but the lizard of Tennessee Williams's play The Night of the ...

explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams's play The Night of the Iguana puts this lizard beside the night.

clue.text: She captured heart of oak, they say

definitions.text: She captured heart of oak, they say

parts.words: She captured heart of oak, they say
parts.note: not naval timber but the heart of Gabriel Oak, the shepherd who loves Hardy's heroine Everdene in Far from the Madding Crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's Bathsheba Everdene wins the devotion of the farmer Gabriel Oak.

clue.text: Foundation member of wins constituency

parts.note: wins as a noun means gains
a borough is a town that once sent members to Parliament, so a constituency

explanation.surface: A founding member of a party takes a winning seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter Gainsborough was one of the founder members of the Royal Academy in 1768; GAINSBOROUGH is also a town in Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was among the original members when the Royal Academy was established in 1768.

clue.text: Bivouacs round university, in its grounds

indicators.note: round says the word for bivouacs goes around the letter for university

parts.note: bivouacs are rough camps

explanation.surface: Students pitch tents around the college grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's grounds, its buildings and land together, form the college estate.

clue.text: "Kindlier touch to her antitheses than pertained to those of that damsel" (Mrs A.D. T. Whitney, The Other Girls)

definitions.text: "Kindlier touch to her antitheses than pertained to those of that damsel" (Mrs A.D. T. Whitney, The Other Girls)

parts.words: "Kindlier touch to her antitheses than pertained to those of that damsel" (Mrs A.D. T. Whitney, The Other Girls)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing before damsel: the adjective, meaning sour or sharp, that describes the unkind girl in Whitney's novel

explanation.walkthrough: The printed quotation lacks its blank; the missing adjective sits before 'damsel', contrasting with the 'kindlier touch'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective for sharp or bitter in temper, the opposite of the kindlier touch in the quotation.

clue.text: He perhaps predictably recognized the cardinal errors of King John

definitions.text: He perhaps predictably recognized the cardinal errors of King John

parts.words: He perhaps predictably recognized the cardinal errors of King John
parts.note: the papal legate who rebukes the king in Shakespeare's history play is a cardinal, so he would spot the king's grave faults

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Pandulph is the papal legate in Shakespeare's King John who excommunicates the king.

clue.text: The land's laid to waste for Henri Beyle

indicators.note: land laid to waste is wrecked, so its letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: The country is ravaged for a Frenchman's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THE LANDS are rearranged; Henri Beyle is the real name of the French novelist who wrote Le Rouge et le Noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie-Henri Beyle published his novels under a pen name, the one in the grid.

clue.text: Source of Charles Morgan

definitions.meaning: a spring or wellhead from which water rises

explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a source of water, and The Fountain is Charles Morgan's best-known novel.

clue.text: A medium performance of Blithe Spirit

definitions.text: A medium performance of Blithe Spirit

parts.words: A medium performance of Blithe Spirit
parts.note: not a middling show but a spiritualist medium's sitting, which Madame Arcati holds in Coward's comedy

explanation.definitionFit: In Noel Coward's Blithe Spirit the medium Madame Arcati holds a sitting to call up the dead.

clue.text: Devious May Day oracle suggests upmarket music school

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A crafty prophecy on the first of May points to a posh conservatoire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Academy of Music in London is a leading conservatoire.

clue.text: Where Eagles Sneer, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the word may be in a different order here

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A twist on the film title Where Eagles Dare.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on Alistair MacLean's Where Eagles Dare; 'Where' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea eagles are called by this short crossword word.

clue.text: Ski jump from Whittier?

parts.note: a ski travels on snow, so it stands for the white stuff
a jump is a bound

explanation.surface: A ski jump taken from an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Greenleaf Whittier, an American poet, wrote Snow-Bound (1866).
explanation.definitionFit: Snow-Bound is Whittier's best-known long poem, about a family cut off by winter.

clue.text: Opera digraph might identify leading character of Buini composition

indicators.note: the letters might, rearranged, name the character, so they are to be shuffled

explanation.surface: Two letters in an opera score point to its hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Maria Buini, an Italian composer, wrote an opera on the Judaean king.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod Agrippa, king of Judaea, is the title role in Buini's opera.

clue.text: Sherwood leading man in historical context

definitions.text: Sherwood leading man in historical context

parts.words: Sherwood leading man in historical context
parts.note: not Robin Hood of Sherwood Forest but the president in Robert E. Sherwood's history ... and Hopkins

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Sherwood's Pulitzer-winning book Roosevelt and Hopkins is a history of the American president and his aide.

clue.text: Pianist blanches in new composition

indicators.note: a new composition puts the letters together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A performer goes pale at a premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Artur Schnabel was an Austrian pianist famed for Beethoven.

clue.text: Anti-hero gives brief news announcement on island

indicators.note: on puts the first piece above the second in this down answer

parts.note: a newsflash is a brief news bulletin
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A villain makes a quick bulletin on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Flashman, bully of Tom Brown's Schooldays, is George MacDonald Fraser's cowardly rogue hero.

clue.text: He may betray his countrymen, like Stevenson, or Lloyd Osbourne

definitions.meaning: one who works with an occupying enemy
Stevenson and his stepson Lloyd Osbourne wrote The Wrong Box and other books together

explanation.definitionFit: A traitor working with an occupier, and a co-writer, as Stevenson and Osbourne were to each other.

clue.text: Amy Myers's master chef acted, that is, right

parts.note: acted means did
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cook performed, so to speak, correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Myers writes detective novels whose sleuth is the Victorian chef Auguste Didier.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Didier, a French cook, is the detective in Amy Myers's series.

clue.text: Twain's visited Camelot

parts.note: Mark Twain's Connecticut man who travels back to King Arthur's court

explanation.definitionFit: Twain's novel A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court sends an American to Camelot.

clue.text: It's not what it was, thought Simone Signoret

definitions.text: It's not what it was, thought Simone Signoret

parts.words: It's not what it was, thought Simone Signoret
parts.note: the French actress titled her memoir with the saying that longing for the past isn't what it used to be

explanation.definitionFit: Signoret's autobiography was called La nostalgie n'est plus ce qu'elle était, about wistful yearning for the past.

clue.text: Discordant gift from Paris

parts.note: not a French present but the golden fruit of discord that Paris of Troy awarded to Aphrodite

explanation.definitionFit: Paris gave the golden fruit inscribed 'to the fairest' to Aphrodite, sparking the Trojan War.

clue.text: Blackmore creation gives point to early Maugham heroine

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
Liza of Lambeth was Maugham's first novel (1897)

explanation.surface: One novelist's character lends sharpness to another's first heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: R.D. Blackmore, author of Lorna Doone, created a character of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name used for a character by the Victorian novelist R.D. Blackmore.

clue.text: Natty sort of woodsman (despite leather stocking)

definitions.text: Natty sort of woodsman (despite leather stocking)

parts.words: Natty sort of woodsman (despite leather stocking)
parts.note: not a smart dresser but Natty, the frontiersman nicknamed Leatherstocking in Fenimore Cooper's tales

explanation.definitionFit: Natty Bumppo, called Leatherstocking, is the hero of Cooper's frontier novels.

clue.text: Well-meaning Italian detective reveals a lover of Beatrice

parts.note: the Italian word meaning well
dick is slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A kindly Italian sleuth turns out to be Beatrice's suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Well-meaning' as 'well, meaning in Italian', not as kindly; Benedick woos Beatrice in Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, Benedick spars with and finally marries Beatrice.

clue.text: Feature of Coleridge's place of confinement

definitions.text: Feature of Coleridge's place of confinement

parts.words: Feature of Coleridge's place of confinement
parts.note: Coleridge's poem calls a bower of lime trees his prison

explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem This Lime-Tree Bower My Prison; the lime is also called by this other tree name.

clue.text: Lydgate's was an Iliad

parts.note: the medieval poet John Lydgate's Troy Book was titled in old spelling as the story of the siege of Troy

explanation.definitionFit: Lydgate's Troy Book was first printed as The Hystorye, Sege and Dystruccyon of Troye, an old spelling for a narrative.
